[p]Hey everyone![/p][p]First thing to note: those of you following updates closely will remember I said the next major content update — [b]Busy Work[/b] — would be coming late September/early October, focusing primarily on new missions. That is still on track.[/p][p]For Busy Work, I did a lot of technical work behind the scenes, which ended up making the game [i]much[/i] better overall. Since so many of these changes improve performance and stability (in some cases even making the game playable for those who struggled before), I decided to release them early as a [b]game health patch[/b] instead of waiting.[/p][p]Alongside performance, I was able to overhaul a lot of the visuals too. Expect [b]dynamic vegetation that reacts to weather, smoother shadows, better colour grading, and more.[/b][/p][p]Another major part of this patch is a complete [b]overhaul of the settings system.[/b] Not only are there now more options to tweak performance and quality, but many things that previously weren’t working correctly — such as vegetation settings, several difficulty options, and more — now function as intended. notes.title: Patch 0.3.6.0 | Tactical Movement
notes.content: [h2]Fargone Patch 0.3.6.0 Release Notes[/h2][p][/p][h3][b]Overview[/b][/h3][p]Patch 0.3.6.0 drops with a completely redesigned character controller system that's genuinely exciting to share with you. This has been months of work rebuilding the movement system from the ground up, and it delivers a significantly enhanced gameplay experience with realistic weight and momentum that creates an almost entirely new feel from the moment you load up the game.[/p][p]Considerable time has also been spent reworking the weapon handling and aiming system to make firearms feel more distinctive and challenging to use. You'll now need to take time to properly line up those long-range shots instead of relying on hip-fire accuracy at extended distances.[/p][p]Looking Ahead: While this update is substantial, work is already deep into preparing version 0.4, which will feature two major additions currently in development:[/p][list][*][p]AI System Overhaul: About 60% complete rebuild using entirely new tools that will finally allow building the AI system that's always been envisioned[/p][/*][*][p]Large-scale Map Refresh: Adding new points of interest and rebuilding existing locations with fresh content[/p][/*][/list][p]This update will combine perfectly with the improved AI of the next patch to bring Fargone up to a much higher level in terms of replayabilityand overall quality. I will be sharing info on patch 0.4 during August with a target of September for release but for now lets dive into what 0.3.6.0 features![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Reworked Movement System[/b][/h3][p]Player Movement 2.0 This was the big focus for this patch. The movement system has been completely rebuilt with proper physics-based foundations. Your character now builds momentum and shifts weight realistically, creating a much more grounded and immersive experience that you'll feel immediately.[/p][p][b]Key Improvements:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Much more stability - you'll rarely get stuck on objects now[/p][/*][*][p]Realistic surface interactions using actual physics calculations[/p][/*][*][p]Dynamic terrain handling that works smoothly across all surface types[/p][/*][*][p]No more unrealistic sliding up vertical surfaces[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Vaulting & Clambering System:[/b] [/h3][p]This is one of the most exciting additions - you can now seamlessly navigate the world by vaulting and clambering over most objects. This system is entirely dynamic, meaning it works across the entire game world as long as the object meets the system requirements.[/p][p][b]What it includes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Works across all world geometry[/p][/*][*][p]Dynamic system that adapts to different objects[/p][/*][*][p]Realistic interaction that feels natural[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]New Sliding Mechanics:[/b] [/h3][p]While sprinting, you can now hit crouch to slide into cover - something that's been wanted for ages. Like the core movement system, this is all physics-based and gets affected by surface type, elevation, your speed, and even your gear weight.[/p][p]Enhanced Leaning System Leaning has been completely reworked to feel much more natural, smooth, and responsive to use.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Visual Effects[/b]: [/h3][p]If you're using vodka to help navigate those radiated zones, you'll now experience a proper drunk effect. Your rads will lower, but it'll come at the cost of struggling to see clearly - so you'll need to decide just how important it is to get that last bit of radiation out of your system! Or if you just want to hang out with Sal and get drunk, that's entirely an option too.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Audio System Overhaul[/b][/h3][p]Player Audio Redesign An entirely new audio system has been built for player sounds, and the difference should be immediately noticeable:[/p][list][*][p]Much Improved Footsteps: Proper surface-specific audio for different terrain types[/p][/*][*][p]Equipment Audio: Your gear will rattle and make movement sounds when you're performing actions and looking around[/p][/*][*][p]Dynamic Breathing: Gradual breathing effects that kick in based on how tired your character is[/p][/*][*][p]Enhanced Action Audio: A whole host of other minor sound tweaks and improvements[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Weapon System Improvements[/b][/h3][p]Realistic Weapon Handling Weapon handling has been fully reworked from the actual physical movement of the weapons themselves. Each gun now moves around far more realistically and feels more unique to use based on various new parameters like gun length, weight, and more.[/p][p]Advanced Aim Sway System This is a new system that's been implemented to make Fargone more realistic than ever before. There's now a subtle shake effect when aiming down iron sights or scopes, and this shake increases the lower your stamina is - meaning aiming after sprinting across half the barrens now comes with a real challenge![/p][p][b]How it works:[/b][/p][list][*][p]You can hold your breath while aiming to stop the shake entirely, but it costs stamina[/p][/*][*][p]There's now a small amount of bullet spread based on whether you're hip firing, aiming, or aiming while holding your breath[/p][/*][*][p]This means taking the time to line up a shot is now important, and hip firing should be more of a notes.title: Development Update & What's Coming Next
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone,[/b]

First off, sorry for being a bit quiet over the past month - I know some of you have been wondering what's happening with development.
I've been dealing with some major changes in my personal life that needed my attention, but these have now been resolved and will actually benefit development time going forward, allowing me to dedicate even more focus to Fargone.
I should have kept you updated during this time, so I wanted to jump back in with a proper development update and let you know what's coming.
I'm committed to being more transparent about development progress going forward. You deserve to know what's happening with the game you've invested in and supported.
What's coming next:
You can expect some smaller updates very soon to address bugs and improvements while I work on the bigger content.
The next major patch is planned for June and will include:

Completely reworked player movement system
New items and equipment
AI follower system - bring companions on your adventures
Base system improvements and new building options
Further AI tweaks and improvements Moving forward:
I'll be keeping you updated more regularly on development progress. Expect to hear from me at least every couple of weeks, whether there's a patch ready or not.

Thank you for your patience and for continuing to support Fargone during early access.
As always, please keep the bug reports and feedback coming - they're invaluable for making the game better.

[b]Thank you for sticking with me and Fargone!

notes.content:
Hey everyone, the new update is live today! Patch 0.3.5.0 titled quarantine zone comes with several requested features such as ammo types, ammo crafting, ammo salvaging, POI enhancements/reworks, new base parts and more.

As promised earlier in the year this update also focuses heavily on polish and has cleaned up many long standing bugs. This will be part of the plan all year ensuring each update is tested thoroughly so please continue to report any issues experienced so that I can make sure they are fixed in future patches.

With all that being said let's jump into some key points for the new update.

[h2]Ammo Crafting[/h2]

One of the main new features of this update is the ability to now craft ammo as well as salvage ammo. New benches can be found in several locations around the world or you can craft them to add to your base. These benches come in 3 tiers, with each tier providing faster crafting/salvage times, different features such as salvaging and also better ammo types such as AP rounds (more ammo types coming very soon!).

To support this system the loot tables have been updated with a range of new items such as casings for each ammo type, gun powder, tungsten (for crafting AP rounds) and more. You can also acquire these materials by salvaging unwanted ammo at any tier 2 or higher ammo bench.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/b7ed051a33bd759c244f2ae9ece1c880ae007460.png[/img]

[h2]Ammo Types[/h2]

As briefly mentioned above this update also introduces a new system for handling multiple ammo types. The introduction of this system comes with only standard and AP rounds for now however the entire ammo system in the background has been rebuilt to support any number of ammo types with unique traits going forward! FMJ and hollowpoint rounds will be coming in a minor update shortly after the release of patch 0.3.5.0.

As an added bonus this ammo rework also fixes a long standing bug of ammo counts being incorrect and some bolt action guns being reloadable infinitely!

[h2]Terrain texture refresh[/h2]

Many of the ground textures in the game have received some added detail through the use of normal maps, texture size increases and refreshed color palettes to give the game a better overall tone. Snow in particular now gets a very nice depth effect during certain lighting conditions/times of day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/89e5ecc697a98e47f2235f91b6dc12cd0897e4d7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/802634a03973d05201b08c612b26d3d70a05470b.png[/img]

[h2]New location & mission[/h2]

With each update I like to try and rework some existing locations that still feature heavy use of synty assets. With this update the quarantine zone has been reworked and also features a brand new mission to hunt down patient 0 and retrieve a sample. This mission can be obtained from Sal after completing the Ran Too Far mission. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/4626378d642e04d16ef6c070829bbd2f010958a0.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e43dc134a5a925e9cf64ae6afe2e7f213ba015f0.png[/img]

[h2]Mission system rework[/h2]

Following on from the above, while creating the new quarantine zone mission, I also fully rebuilt the mission system. As many have pointed out, not many new missions have been added to the game during its release in early access, this is because quite frankly the mission system was hard to extend in its old state. The new system is not only much easier to work with but also far more stable meaning you should have a much smoother experience when playing the current set of missions. New missions including the first chapter of the main story will also now be making their way into the game later this year.

[h2]Loose loot rework[/h2]

One of the things often mentioned in terms of feedback is the lack of things to loot, with this update I have built a new loose loot system meaning a far greater number of things will spawn in random places to be picked up. This currently only affects newer areas such as the quarantine zone but I am already working to extend it to all existing locations too! In fact many locations in the mountain areas have received the new loot system already.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/d247e1fbb2656936b5d03f51185069f1ce9e685b.png[/img]

notes.title: Fargone in 2025 - The Mission
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone,[/b]
I hope you all had a fantastic Christmas and New Year!

2024 was a milestone year for Fargone. With the addition of base building, new locations, the bunker system, lots of new items, a new faction and tons more, the game is edging closer to the ultimate vision I’ve been striving for.

That said, I want to be honest with you all: this year came with its challenges. As a solo developer, balancing development, personal life, and a major disruption in my own life was tough. I also want to give a special shoutout to Sadlife on Discord, our incredible 3D artist, whose work has been instrumental in moving the game away from asset dependency.

These experiences taught me a lot about time management and development practices. I’m confident these lessons will lead to a smoother development process in 2025, with more content and fewer bugs. The work I’ve been doing behind the scenes has set us up for a strong year ahead, and I’m genuinely excited for what’s to come.

[b]2025 Roadmap[/b]
Let’s talk about the roadmap.
While 2024’s roadmap didn’t entirely go as planned, the lessons I’ve learned have informed how I’m approaching this year. A new roadmap is coming soon, incorporating content originally planned for 2024 plus some exciting new additions. However, I won’t assign specific quarters for updates this time. Flexibility in scheduling will help ensure updates are better tested and polished before release.

[b]Addressing Bugs[/b]
Bugs are one area I’m determined to tackle head-on in 2025.
I know many of you have faced issues, and I take full responsibility for the impact this has had on your experience. Balancing new content with polish has been a challenge, but I’m committing to making 2025 the year of stability. I’ve already compiled a list of issues to address and implemented a new internal testing procedure to minimize bugs in future updates. While bugs are an inevitable part of game development, I’m dedicated to reducing their frequency and impact moving forward.

[b]Exciting Content in 2025[/b]
Now, onto the fun part: content!
This year, you can expect vehicles—a highly requested feature—to finally make their debut. Additionally, content originally planned for 2024 will also be rolling out, alongside brand-new surprises. I’ll share more about the roadmap soon once I’m happy with its direction.

[b]Multiplayer Plans[/b]
I know multiplayer, particularly co-op, is a big topic for the community.
While I agree that multiplayer will elevate Fargone to new heights, it’s crucial to ensure the game is stable and content-rich first. Adding multiplayer would require a significant development effort and could halt progress in other areas temporarily. Additionally, it would introduce its own set of challenges and bugs.

Here’s the good news: multiplayer is not abandoned. The game has been built with multiplayer in mind from the start, and I’ve been in discussions with a developer about prototyping co-op. While I don’t have concrete plans yet, it’s something I’m actively exploring.

[b]Thank You[/b]
To everyone who’s been part of this journey, you’ve made a dream come true.
Your support, feedback, bug reports, and suggestions mean the world to me and directly contribute to making Fargone a better experience. I can’t thank you enough for being part of this community and sticking with me.

2025 is going to be Fargone’s best year yet. I can’t wait to share more with you and see you all in The Barrens!

Thank you again for everything.

notes.title: Patch 0.3.4.0 | Homesteaders
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/c145f9a26b43c2381fe4ab28c19ed220e0c142ba.png[/img]

Hey everyone, I know this one has been a long time coming. A lot of things have changed internally, which I’ve communicated on Discord but not here. I usually try to reserve Steam posts for actual content, so if you want to stay updated more regularly, please feel free to join the Discord channel!

As many of you have noticed, the roadmap will need a refresh. A mixture of personal issues and this update being far, FAR more complicated than anticipated has led to some internal shakeups. The good news is that there’s a solid plan for 2025 that will allow me to get content out much faster, bringing the game closer to the vision I have for it!

Another thing to note, usually when I release a major update the game will go on sale, as the winter sale is only a few days away I am unable to do a specific update sale however the game will be going on sale in 3 days as part of the steam winter sale so keep an eye out in a few days if you are looking to pickup the game!

Thank you for all the support and for bearing with me through these quiet months. I hope this update gives you all lots of new content to enjoy until the next one!

[h2]Base Building[/h2]

The main focus of this update is a full base building system. This has been talked about and requested since the day the game launched, and I’m extremely happy to finally provide it and do it justice. There are lots of options to help you create the perfect base!

Base building features lots of prefabs that can be snapped together such as foundations, walls, ceilings, support beams, stairs and more. The range of available base parts will also be expanded as this is now going to be a core pillar of the game so expect extensions and improvements to this system as we go forward.

With the new map improvements (explained in more detail below) you can also now name each base and see it on the map to allow for easy management of multiple bases. To make all these features work you do now need to place down a base computer to begin building most items, this is a change from the old system in which you could place items freely anywhere however to handle the size of the new base system and all the new features a base computer is required to allow the game to know where to trigger events and also cull items for performance when leaving a base.

You are also now able to craft useful utilities such as a rain catcher that supplies fresh water over time, radio towers allowing the Runners to offer fast travel services to your base and much more.

This update features the most handcrafted set of assets to date. Once again, this is a push to move away from store-bought assets like Synty and give Fargone much more of its own identity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/2283fbf70b2599a658333632c270c24d7a387dff.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/61e1f39431d9fe781a55ce91e5eab9321e2430ac.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ec877de60b1b0e0b48d92296ccf7c0cbfe2722ac.png[/img]

[h2]Wandering Trader[/h2]

A new wandering trader can currently be found in the mountains, with more coming to other areas of the map shortly. The wandering trader specializes in base building materials and parts, allowing those of you with spare cash quick access to essential items for diving into the new base building content.

As always, you can scavenge for parts and materials too, giving you multiple options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5a8348d7f90dd7a800b1c2c1fb3abf8f5e84f305.png[/img]

[h2]Map Improvements[/h2]

The map has been something many have had issues with, and for good reason—it was not hugely useful. While even more improvements are coming in the next update, maps in Homesteaders now provide proper UI icons for notable locations such as traders, mission locations, safe zones, and more. You can also hover over these icons to see additional information about a marker. Additionally, you can now click on mission markers directly from the map to update your currently tracked quest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/3dea2744c5609a00e1cb59f01b2b631ea8a864f5.png[/img]

[h2]Vegetation Rework[/h2]

Vegetation has been fully rebuilt to provide better visuals and performance. The new vegetation also includes features such as interactive grass that reacts to player collision and weather. You will also now see dynamic puddles form based on the current weather conditions. Together, these features add a new level of believability to the world of The Barrens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/72d082a5e1547d77bbc6500b64c39d984552e223.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/d173dd906873d80b7eb3af46d34fd07391918735.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/631b261a6655b96da944a0167290b4db77b5f188.png[/img]

[h2]Cooking & Buff Improvements[/h2]

The cooking system has been fully remade to provide a much cleaner, easier-to-read menu that is also more expandable for future recipes. This update includes several new recipes, such as herbal teas that offer different boosts and the ability to cook zombie arms for food if you find yourself in a bad situation!

Additionally, improvements have been made to the buff system. You can now hover over a buff or debuff icon in the inventory screen to see exactly how much time is left. This works particularly well with the new herbal teas, which offer effects like increased carry capacity for an hour.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/8ffc892712e6af9f2fbbca1773265fd73eb75996.png[/img]

[h2]Gathering[/h2]

To support the new recipes, such as herbal teas, many plants can now be harvested around the world and serve as essential ingredients.

[h2]Final Notes[/h2]

There are two planned minor updates that will extend this update and arrive shortly after. These will add the remaining planned features, such as full zombie and bandit invasions, supply routes to towns for your bases, and ammo crafting. Many of these features are already close to completion, so these extension updates won’t be far behind. After that, the refreshed roadmap will be the priority.

notes.title: Patch 0.3.3.0 | Open Warfare PT 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/05fa691fd64c86d22628ce63fa1c5bdc3b7d31d8.png[/img]

Hey everyone, Open Warfare Part 2 is finally here! This update has taken a while as I wanted to spend more time incorporating player feedback and refining the game. This update also includes a large new area to explore (The Plains), a new faction called Liberty, and many other features such as new defense events, new loot, enemies, and more. Players who explored this area back in Legacy will notice significant changes, offering a completely fresh experience!

This update also brings with it some major balance changes that significantly improve the feeling of progression. Weapon stats, consumables, and shop prices have all been polished and refined.

The full raw patch notes can be found at the bottom of this post. This update is currently being deployed and should be available on steam withing the next 24 hours.

[h2]Plains (New Zone)[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/b976285ff9fc383349a84a4a37a8221367faea66.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/6d963b1497cca2f91355858b097b3096041e7055.png[/img]

Open Warfare Part 2 brings back the long-awaited Plains zone. Almost every location has been updated and improved with greater detail. You will find a greater number of unique AI spawns, many lootable POIs, and much more.

The unique quest line to build a Liberty Heavy suit also returns, allowing players to work towards obtaining one of the best (and coolest) armor sets in the game.

The Plains also feature regular faction skirmishes between the Military and Liberty, with Bandits occasionally getting involved.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/9aa774ac5e129f559f69ada152440b67defdace1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/f33eee396b26fda16a0e5afdbdd57b5a969bc9cd.png[/img]

[h2]AI Combat Improvements[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/8c2829fdf2e9dd299c2fa0d722231bbad2bc67c5.png[/img]

The Plains is a dangerous place, and Liberty, in particular, is a tough opposition for most players who have not worked to gain their trust. AI combat has been greatly improved, allowing better utilization of cover, combat movement, and aiming. This results in longer and more engaging firefights, both AI vs. AI and Player vs. AI.

[h2]New Enemies[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/b021817c4d126d65cb169a23404f17d5ae625433.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/76164919a60b7ebba6865ac5f0912574b65d467a.png[/img]

This update introduces two new enemy types: the Exploder and the Armored Zombie. As the name suggests, the Exploder charges the player and triggers a large explosion when in range, damaging anything within its radius. The Armored Zombie, though a rare spawn, requires more than a simple headshot to defeat.

Additionally, Husks now emit a small amount of radiation, which can stack when several husks attack together. This is made possible with the new radiation system explained further down.

[h2]Defense Missions[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/447223bbd745a7b6192fcdd72aeaf7145d04693c.png[/img]

A new world event can be discovered in several locations around the Plains. These Liberty experiments can be activated by the player, sending out a signal that attracts specific types of undead and mutants. Players who survive these events can either loot the cache that unlocks upon completion or donate the cache to Liberty in exchange for reputation.

[h2]Equipment[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e2a29466ac094e766e485d644c4a5e2c123685e7.png[/img]

Grenades, Molotovs, and chem lights have been added back into the game, expanding the options players have when engaging in combat or exploring dark environments.

Additionally, Molotovs can now set undead on fire within a radius, making them exceptionally good for taking down large clusters of undead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/be5f67973bb61a3449a65cfa645269b532a87ef9.png[/img]

[h2]QoL and Improvements[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5a670494dbfe57532dc5b3607f25ddd2c3e9199b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/8703974a3a57b031b7949acc1f202699dbb25f1d.png[/img]

Patch 0.3.3 brings several highly requested features, such as a loot all button and inventory autosorting. Players can also bring their weapons to a new NPC in the Sub-0 bar to get them repaired to a level of their choosing for a price.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/bac68edd5fbd209b295f2e5abd526226ee5024f7.png[/img]

AI that are killed will now also drop their weapons on the ground, which can then be picked up/looted. AI bodies and their loot now persist when saving and reloading the game.

As with every patch, numerous bugs have been fixed along with general optimizations and improvements. Full patch notes below.

Another improvement requested for some time now is the display of character customization and equipment within the main menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5a7430b589ca16850c1bd6208c187f507fccdf88.png[/img]

[h2]What's Next?[/h2]

The next big update is already planned, and details will be shared in the coming weeks. This one is going to be a pretty big one!

Additionally, an official road map will be released in the next few weeks. Up until now, I have kept many plans close to my chest, but I feel the game is now in a solid place where I can start to reveal what's coming for the rest of the year and beyond.

As always, thank you to everyone who has played and supported the game! You are making a solo dev's dreams a reality, and I can't thank you all enough!

[h2]Patreon Rewards[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ae31b370825e91317b8c25e5c897368e6c3992c6.png[/img]

This section is for those who have been supporting the game on Patreon for a long time and have been awaiting your first reward drop. You now have access to some unique skins for the Ret 51 sniper, which also features some very nice cloth-based physics for the wrap!

These can be unlocked from the main menu using your code and then applied at the new weapon workshop NPC.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/653f6a58afc529b922d61a0e7c8c6beab93d6538.png[/img]

Hey everyone, I am excited to announce the next content patch for Fargone titled Open Warfare. This patch will be a 2 part update with part 1 launching later today and part 2 later in the week. 

This update brings with it lots of improvements to AI, as well as new activities, items, and more.

[h2]Bunker 27 (End game activity)[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/f3ca98041987e224779fde4542daaec8ca403f4f.png[/img]

Open Warfare introduces the first of the bunkers, these are designed to be hard end game activities with high risk and high rewards. To access the bunkers you must first defeat one of the new brute bosses to obtain a key card which can then be decoded at the Bunker Master to gain a usable key to unlock the bunker door. When inside you will be unable to save the game or build base parts, death will also result in you losing all items currently in your inventory so preparation is key.

Inside you will find one of Fargones most highly detailed and atmospheric locations to date featuring scripted events, new interactive objects such as keypads and tons of lore which is now logged in your data pad allowing you to read what you have found in order to help you escape.

The goal is to locate and extract locked crates from within the bunker which can then be returned to the bunker master to be opened. The bunker system is designed to be a repeatable end game activity, with more bunkers coming in future updates.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5442e317399a6c2280171ad6fd01028c9bd96ff2.png[/img]

[h2]New & Enhanced AI[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5e1c042b41062596d9a4a215c525380c8d52be5b.png[/img]

Firstly, the brute boss is back, and he throws rocks now... As mentioned above you will need to defeat a brute in order to obtain bunker access cards.

Human AI has seen a large number of improvements as well as a few new additions. 

NPC's will now be far more tactical when in a firefight, often seeking cover when under threat, needing to reload or many other scenarios where they feel under pressure. NPCs also have a few new voice varieties as well as many more unique spoken lines based on different situations in and out of combat.

There is also a far greater number of spawns across the map from static camps to roaming patrols fighting along the roads. The goal is to increase the amount of activity happening across the map making things feel far more alive. 

Finally a new wounding system has been added to human NPC's, this system allows the player the choice to help or executing downed NPC's. Helping an NPC will also grant a small boost to the faction of the NPC.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/115921318a8878115ef0251888f408ef217aed06.png[/img]

[h2]New Items[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/1a93daeebca25bd5cc241af8055042836494c89c.png[/img]

This update also features the first of the new style of guns, the tactical M4. This gun features the most detailed model in game along with vastly improved animations to complement it. The tactical m4 also features several unique attachments dubbed Gen 2, which is a part of a greater set of equipment linked to some experimental work by the Military. The tactical M4 and it's attachments can be found in the locked crates extracted from Bunker 27.

Along with this, new outfits have been added for the player to obtain for each of the different bandit tiers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/8b44aeb0dd73d3ac2e078f609f25b947862a60ad.png[/img]

As mentioned above, part 2 for this update will launch later this week with a separate set of patch notes, I hope you all enjoy the new content and thank you again for playing Fargone!

Hey everyone!

Patch 0.3.1.0 has arrived, marking the first content update since the release of 0.3. This update brings a significant overhaul to the progression system, a feature I've been eager to implement for quite some time. Drawing inspiration from typical RPG skill trees, the new progression system in Fargone aims for realism. Each skill has been carefully designed to make sense within the game world, ensuring balance without sacrificing the excitement of unlocking new abilities.

Additionally, this patch includes numerous bug fixes, enhancements to lighting, and performance improvements, further refining the player experience.

Thank you to everyone who has been part of the Fargone community and contributed to its development. Regular bug fixes and smaller patches will continue as regularly as they have been and the next update is planned for early April and will feature some significant new content to play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e3ae91da4692ce0f32d0f9bb46b2572e94505c7c.png[/img]

[b][h2]Skill tree[/h2][/b]

The XP system has been reintroduced alongside a completely revamped skill tree system, providing plenty of choices to build out your character in unique ways. With three trees—Survivalist, Scavenger, and Fighter—each featuring four tiers, there are a total of 24 skills to unlock.

Each tree represents a distinct playstyle, offering players the opportunity to specialize in survival, scavenging, or combat. Within each tier, players must choose between two skills, emphasizing balance while ensuring that progression feels realistic—you can't become a master of everything (most likely)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/a900f8385f0b3f920f0fcb24caf25282d06d3529.png[/img]

In addition to the skill system, new AI spawns have been introduced, along with a new warehouse POI located in the mountains, replacing the old one found during the "Ran Too Far" mission. Night vision goggles have undergone an overhaul, making them far more useful. Color grading has been reworked to create brighter and clearer daytimes, while bloom implementation has also been reworked, enhancing the visuals and atmosphere of the game even further.

notes.title: Patch 0.3 | New Beginnings
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Everyone![/h2]
I'm thrilled to announce the upcoming release of [b]Patch 0.3: New Beginnings[/b] for Fargone! This update represents a monumental step forward for the game with almost 60% of the code base being rewritten. With so much changing behind the scenes this post will showcase most of the major changes that will impact the gameplay most. Patch 0.3 will be releasing next week on December 22nd.

[h2]A Heartfelt Thanks:[/h2]
A huge thank you to everyone for being so patient with me while working on this update, I know it's taken a while! I'm excited to return to a rhythm of more frequent and substantial updates now that 0.3 is done.

[h2]Diving Into the Highlights[/h2]

[h3]AI 2.0[/h3]
This update kicks off the launch of the new AI system I have been working on for a while. AI 2.0's biggest strength is in the ability to add to it and improve it as time goes on. The old AI system was not only inadequate but also nearly impossible to work on. This new system has been rewritten from the ground up and, while this is the initial launch of the new system, it is already miles better than the old one. Prepare for more active and dynamic AI that will attempt to flush you out of cover, take cover themselves, and work with each other to gain the upper hand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ecd8b840a3bd2fcbb3a3a97486166624f13ca734.png[/img]

[h3]Inventory Overhaul[/h3]
Following your feedback, the inventory system has been entirely reworked. The new custom grid system not only enhances the visual appeal but also streamlines inventory management, making it more intuitive and user-friendly. Whether you’re sorting loot, organizing gear, or browsing shops, the experience is fluid and satisfying.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e61e0756823a5bb65e93e7503299610e7eadbb1d.png[/img]

[h3]New Character Equipment System[/h3]
The revamped modular character system is a game-changer, allowing players to fully customize their characters. This system empowers you to express your style, whether it’s mixing and matching different outfit pieces or completing a coveted set. The hunt for the perfect look is as exciting as the gameplay itself. With the new modular pieces being distributed throughout the loot system, it brings the total number of items to nearly 300!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ef6ffcc1234a9d0c609351ed2117149e8abd78fe.png[/img]

[h3]Reworked Attachment System[/h3]
Crafting benches are now gone since crafting a holographic sight with some wire and metal seemed very strange! Attachments are now part of the world like any other item, they can be bought from vendors, looted from containers or from dead enemies. You can now also store these attachments in your backpack and swap them out on the fly from within your inventory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/3d216fe80d43710cbf180fcabbae549b63e2d147.png[/img]

[h3]Character Redesign[/h3]
Stepping away from Synty assets, the characters have been remodeled and retextured. This includes a diverse range of AI and zombie characters, all benefiting from the new modular system. The result is a more unique and visually compelling game world.

[h3]Weapon Overhauls[/h3]
Every gun in Fargone has been retextured and also received an entirely new audio system. In particular, distant gunshots now actually sound realistic, you will hear distant snaps and cracks as AI far away deal with their own situations adding to the atmosphere of the game. Many of the weapons have also received a greater number of available attachments to apply as well, opening up more options for your loadout.

[h3]Barrens Local Network System[/h3]
Immerse yourself deeper into the game world with the Barrens local network system. It keeps you informed of in-game events like shop restocks and toxic storms, adding a layer of strategic depth and enhancing the sense of a living, breathing world. AI will also send messages to each other requesting help or just general chit chat. This system is the first version and it will also be expanded going forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/4d5ccb8472e0a5d85a8716ebaf17e79b32624f9a.png[/img]

[h3]Graphical Enhancements[/h3]
Several areas of the game have received graphical improvements, but the most noteworthy is a new volumetric light scattering effect. This effect looks particularly good during toxic storms as you will see green flashes of light pour through windows as the storm outside rages on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/9f763ff0a3bf95a7126376469580ed67663117c2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ae0be5542f19457f07658e2a27e6e0bbd1a718f6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/0b295d89ad0a81bc1aecc38352393ab829780406.png[/img]

[h3]Customizable Difficulty[/h3]
Responding to popular demand, I've added customizable difficulty settings. Now, you can fine-tune various aspects like enemy accuracy and loot frequency to create a gameplay experience that matches your preferences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/a72c2b96b28ce8fa6e1881a441910951f7ec8458.png[/img]

[h3]General Player Improvements[/h3]
Every aspect of the player experience has been enhanced. New animations for consumable items add to the realism, while the ability to move while consuming items increases fluidity in gameplay. The first-person view and lighting response have also been refined for a more immersive feel.

[h3]Optimisations[/h3]
This update brings with it a host of optimisations to increase performance and lower resource use. In particular, I am targeting making the game run better on the Steam Deck. This update is part 1 of a large optimisation project I am doing for the game, bringing in all the knowledge I have gained building this game to improve the experience.

[h2]And There's So Much More...[/h2]
This update, touching nearly 60% of the game's code, is just the beginning. It lays the groundwork for faster, more efficient future development and paves the way for exciting new content.

[h2]Stay Tuned[/h2]
I'm already hard at work on the next batch of content, so stay alert for future announcements. For now, delve into the detailed patch notes below for a complete overview of all the new changes and enhancements.

New Features

notes.title: Fargone Devlog #1
notes.content:
Hi everyone, I know it has been a while since the last post so I appreciate everyone being patient with me. With patch 0.3 growing into almost a second launch for the early access version of Fargone I have decided to start doing some develops that I will be posting every 2 weeks regardless of other announcements or sharing of new features.

So the big question is, why is patch 0.3 taking so long!? Well, this update has become huge internally. This patch has grown into a soft re-launch of the game for me. Not saying there was anything wrong with the original launch however there were many things that I did not get time to do in the way I wanted and many features that were either missing or not completed fully. So, let's get into what I have been working on in its entirety since the last post.

This post is a continuation of the previouse patch 0.3 post so if you have not read that yet you can find it here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2242100/view/5868803522304295947?l=english

[h2]A rework of the entire code base and toolset surrounding items[/h2]

This may not seem exciting on the surface however it is major for ensuring the long-term health of the game. A big issue I have had for some time is how items were originally created. The system was tedious, and difficult to manage and made managing items both time-consuming and also very error-prone. The new system allows for easy mass management of every item in the game, allowing me to add, edit or delete any item in the game within seconds. This is part of my plan to ensure the game is easier to work on going forward making for faster updates.

Whilst working in this area I have also added an entire new loot spawning system. Loot is now randomised far better and spawns more frequently both in containers and on the ground. This can also be adjusted by the new difficulty settings announced previously. Also, loot now has a new rarity attached to each item which is color-coded allowing for a bit more excitement when looting those cool rarer items! Hovering over an item will now change the tooltip header to display the rarity colour.

[h2]UI tweaks & refresh and inventory rework[/h2]

A big change that is currently being worked on is a new grid-style inventory system. This is something I have liked the idea of for some time and am very happy to finally bring to the game. Storing items will now be a small mini-game in a way as opposed to a simple hard limit on the number of slots. This feature is still early on as reworking the inventory is a huge task but progress is good!

Another thing I have been working on is refreshing various parts of the UI starting with the base font. I have had a lot of feedback in regard to the font so have adjusted several text-heavy areas with a new clearer font. The tooltip window and context menu have also been cleaned up and although small, these little bits add up to make for an overall better experience.

Here is a WIP preview of the new grid system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/dc4a1d92933bff8ad10c5c2237abecaea483a170.png[/img]

[h2]Weapon retexture project[/h2]

I have announced this already but it has now been finished so I wanted to share some of the amazing work done to the weapons in the game. These textures fit much better with the gritty atmosphere that the game has been striving for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/51bd7ab7dc6fa6c8b22cd5d5971fe462dcee7e66.png[/img]

[h2]Barrens local network system[/h2]

Here is something I am very excited about! The Barrens local network has received a major update allowing for dynamic messages to be posted by the AI that inhabits the world. You will now receive messages from actual AI nearby to warn you of things such as incoming toxic weather, shops getting a stock refresh, certain special enemies being spotted or just general messages asking for help when under attack and much more. This is a feature I wanted for some time and it adds another level of depth to the AI making the world truly feel alive and that things are happening around the player without their direct involvement. You can also view a full log of recent messages in a new tab within the datapad.

The datapad is also due for a major rework however I am not quite ready to share too much since the new artwork has been completed and it has been planned but I have yet to implement it into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/5987732092d8426dde820291d4de19283ce90462.png[/img]

[h2]Visual & audio improvements[/h2]

Another thing coming which I want to give a quick mention is some visual and audio changes. The first is a new procedural lightning technique that has been added to the game bringing a bit more atmosphere to storms, a small feature but one I personally love.

As well as this I have been working on improving certain audio features such as the sound detection method for which footstep audio should play. This has long been broken and often would play the wrong sounds. I am also looking at making some changes to the weapon sounds however this has not yet been started.

[h2]What's next?[/h2]

Well, that wraps up a lot of what I have been working on so far, the rework of the item code has been a major undertaking and I can't stress how important it will be going forward for the game. I still have lots of unannounced and planned content for this patch that I will update as time goes on. This patch will still take a tad longer and I am sorry for that however I promise it will be worth it once it drops and future content will come out faster as a result of this update. The core of the game is being rewritten in lots of ways to create a new foundation with patch 0.3. The idea is going forward updates will be far more structured and content-packed.

I know many will want to know a release date and I am not quite there yet, just know my plans are for this not to be a million miles away. A month or two would be a realistic target without setting a concrete date. I will be sharing more info and dev logs regularly so keep an eye out and as always thank you very much for the support and for playing Fargone!

notes.title: Upcoming features in patch 0.3
notes.content:
Hi everyone, I wanted to take a moment today to discuss the planned content for patch 0.3. This update is still heavy in development so some content may be subject to change or moved around.

Patch 0.3 is focused on expanding what is already in game as opposed to an entirely new area as with Unknown Origins. The idea is to add more flexibility to player customisation, flesh out some features already in game that need a second pass, add some new locations to the existing world space and improve the overall feeling of progression in the game. Below I will list several but NOT all of the points being focused on to achieve this. More details will be shared soon as I now begin the build up to releasing this update.

[h2]Difficulty Options/h2]

The first thing to go over with patch 0.3 is the option to adjust various settings to tweak the games difficulty. You will be able to adjust several values such as toxic storm damage, loosing items on death, loot chances, damage values and more. This has been heavily requested since day 1 so I am very excited to be able to allow you all to tweak the game for a better experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ea8853e8da3dc02d0c47f4d4e2eb3e9f0feca97a.png[/img]

[h2]AI 2.0[/h2]

I have never shied away from the flaws of the current AI system. They have needed a second pass for some time and this is a feature I have been talking about for some time. This is currently planned for patch 0.3 and lots of time has already been put into it however due to the size of this task there is the possibility of it being pushed back slightly if it ends up holding back all the other content for too long. That being said let's talk AI 2.0. I will be breaking down each of the modules and explaining how they have been improved.

AI Life / Idle

Currently AI life and idle is very simple. If they are wandering the map they will simply pick a point and go in a straight line towards it. With the new system, they now will plot unique patrol paths that can weave through POIs and other interesting locations. You will see AI potentially plotting a path into a building mid-patrol to rest and overall have AI that roams the world more believably.

AI Combat 

The big one, ai combat. Currently, AI has tons of issues in combat ranging from running away too easily, getting stuck not shooting, inconsistent weapon condition firing ability and clipping through the floor and walls.

It's hard to break down exactly what's going to be new with this because everything will be new. This is being rewritten from scratch and I think the best thing will be for me to show it in action closer to the time. Just know, it will be ALOT better!

[h2]Reworked customisation[/h2]

With patch 0.3 the player model has been rebuilt from scratch. The reason behind this was to offer greater flexibility with equipment. With the current version of the game, you can equip a helmet, mask and an outfit. With the new version, you will able to equip individual pieces such as gloves, pants, tops and boots in combination with the existing helmet and mask options. This will allow for a far greater number of options for the player's equipment and will also expand loot options. This is one of the changes I am personally excited for most since the current system is heavily limited by the use of assets early in development so with the new system being built for Fargone I have far more control going forward as well as a being able to create far better and more unique outfits going forward.

[h2]Attachement system 2.0[/h2]

Patch 0.3 will also introduce what I am calling attachments 2.0. The primary focus for this is to overhaul how the player goes about fitting attachments to weapons. I find the current implementation to not work as well as I originally planned by forcing the player to craft attachments at benches and to only have one attachment per slot at a time. While the new system is still being worked on and may change, the current idea is to move attachments away from the crafting bench and integrate them into the world. You will now be able to loot and buy attachments at which point they will be stored in your inventory as opposed to going straight onto the weapon. You can then drag and drop these attachments onto either your primary or secondary to either equip or swap them out. Your old attachments will be returned to your backpack. This will allow players to bring a set of attachments and weapons with them to prepare for different engagements and again will offer greater flexibility.

On top of this, a new scope system has been implemented to make scopes look far more realistic and clear incorporating a new 'true 3d' effect to the scopes. Some weapons will also be receiving new attachments or a greater number of options for attachments.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExbTVyeWZ6Zm52dWhsdGN0aTZvNW01ZXNmNm00YTczamlvMXgzNDFnbCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/aD4OJMCl94TOycOQdq/giphy.gif[/img]

[h2]Hordes/h2]

Zombie hordes can now roam the world at random. Hordes can happen in one of two ways, they can either spawn at a random or can be triggered by heavy amounts of noise in a certain area. If NPC's or the player get into a large fight near a POI a zombie horde could begin to form and approach the area adding another layer of depth to open world engagements. Hordes range between 20-40 zombies and mutants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ab8dce48613e89906dd7209c63db3fe90a2e5786.png[/img]

[h2]Bunker system 1.0[/h2]

As you may know, there is a bunker in the game with a system built around it to allow the player to unlock it. This was planned to be a far bigger system than what is currently in the game. With patch 0.3 the first proper bunker will be added to the game. With long tunnels connecting to a variety of rooms, platforms and levels, this bunker is designed to be a mini dungeon-type activity which will test the player in return for high-level rewards and even a few bunker-specific uniques. There will be many more bunkers in the future including replacing the current one however I think you are all going to love what has been done for the first full bunker.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/021e9d0f404ed141ec9c6d6dbcb142a93c088a6a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e75266f8e8a82c9cfc13e66774473ed0f327eac3.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/cc72bc8ae416f852a4dc530a09fdabb1847af664.png[/img]

[h2]Progression[/h2]

The current skill point system is very simple and most players even forget to use it. Going forward this system will be entirely replaced with a new talent/skill system in which players can unlock skills with different effects to better create a build that suits their play style. Additionally, I am looking at whether or not to entirely replace the level/xp system with something more interesting.

On top of this, I would like to expand the faction system to have ranks as well that you earn by helping your faction. These ranks will unlock new items and support options from your current faction. This feature is still in its planning phase but is something I will be beginning work on soon!

[h2]Steam Achievements[/h2]

Following progression, I will also be implementing the first set of Steam achievements. These have already been created internally and will be implemented with patch 0.3.

[h2]More to come soon...[/h2]

I have other things planned and even being developed for this update and will be sharing more info soon. As for the release, I will not be committing to a date just set like before as I don't want to create pressure and instead want to release this patch in its best form when ready.

Thank you for taking the time to read this and also for playing the game, talk again soon!

notes.title: Unknown Origins PT 1 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hey there, it's finally time to lift the curtain on the full patch notes for Unknown Origins Part 1 launching tomorrow! (Friday 26th). The game will also be going on sale when the update launches tomorrow. 

You can read a full list of the patch notes at the bottom of the page but first I want to highlight some of the big features of this update.

[h2]Overhauled immersion[/h2]

For this update I have spent a lot of time focusing on improving the level of quality found in terms of graphics, audio improvements, weather improvements, general ambience, lighting and much more. All of these combine together to create a far more immersive environment then ever before. 3D audio has been adjusted for a range of sounds meaning characters and undead will now be audible at a realistic level in relation to their distance from the player. General ambience has been overhauled with new dynamic tracks playing depending on which zone the player is in as well as the time of day. 

Lighting has been massively improved. you will now see better volumetric lighting effects, improved sky colours throughout the day, darker and more immersive night time, lighting flashes during acid storms and much more. Nothing beats wandering through an acid storm in darkness while hearing the distant screams of the undead wondering where your next safe stop might be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/36a205e6c0240da9ba0aff055b0f56972b1d7b3f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/be1ec0e727fb509f77b350649b202e92a64bd124.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/14657d94a71adb05ec72fa200b5db2cc19565963.png[/img]

[h2]Voice acting[/h2]

Unknown Origins begins implementing something I have wanted for some time, voice acting. For now this is limited to dynamic world AI and not story characters. You will now hear AI reacting to being shot, covering each other, shouting words of encouragement, taunts or cry's for help as a nearby ally falls. Liberty will have their own unique radio static voice lines to reflect the often covered up helmets they wear. AI will also have a variety of greeting voice lines when starting a conversation.

[h2]Runners Travel Service[/h2]

You can now pay any Runner found out in the world a sum of credits for safe passage to a variety of locations across the Barrens. Need to get to the new Plains area but find yourself stuck far away? Find a Runner and get there fast and safely.

[h2]New gear and characters[/h2]

Equip yourself with a variety of weapons and gear used by members of Liberty. New crates can be found around the Plains containing tons of new loot including new weapons, the P90, MK14, G36C and the M22 heavy machine gun. You can also find 3 new Liberty suits and 4 new Liberty helmets.

[h2]New enemies and dangers[/h2]

A new weather type can happen at random across the Barrens, the acid storm. In order to survive this new environmental threat you must either equip yourself with protective gear or find shelter, alternatively you can just keep chugging alcohol to lower your toxicity levels! Speaking of toxicity, infection is a new value that can now be impacted by taking damage from undead characters. High infections levels will impact your characters overall health and extremely high levels will incur periodic health loss. Combat this new danger with antibiotics also added in this update. As well as all this you will now have to deal with dangerous mutants that now inhabit the world as well making the Barrens more dangerous than ever before.

[h2]New features and QOL's[/h2]

With the new update you must now consider the weight of your equipment as your backpack is no longer the only thing that can slow you down. Equipping heavy armour may make you far more likely to survive a long range shot however it will come at the cost of your ability to move quickly. The idea behind this is to begin adding more reasons to mix and match gear for different situations. 

A new largely requested QOL now added is the ability to see what attachments are equipped to a weapon from within the inventory. This will make it easier when sorting through stashed weapons or selling items to know which are your most important weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/46f93b3051b5f15d9d6aabc142b13a8e51be0069.png[/img]

[h2]A huge amount of new locations[/h2]

This update brings with it the largest expansion of explorable locations to date with a large new terrain exactly half the size of the base game map that contains over a dozen new POI's ranging from small encampments to large sprawling train-yards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/1d9ea736cd0745e64ea02012aa51375f86a12283.png[/img]

[h2]New weapons, animations & legendary gear[/h2]

Continuing from Trials Of The Hollowed, the remaining weapons have received the revamped animations and in some cases audio treatment bringing them up to standard with the rest. As well as this both unarmed and melee weapons have received reworked animations. On top of this several new weapons have been added in both the gun and melee categories. You can also hunt down a selection of new legendary items such as the guarded axe, commanders slasher and a range of rare masks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/1956db72e62f354b459808470fa39dd1d71f69b8.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/a980e2a4e90a87e4343ea0ba4b562e0f4f361c47.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/3d8a6bac2b9b938fe0d71197638f9ddde9556d87.png[/img]

[h2]New quests[/h2]

With the release of part 1 quests were not the primary focus however that being said this update still doubles the count of available quests in game. Part 2 will have a larger focus on quests and will be right around the corner but for now you can complete a long quest chain to build the legendary Liberty Elite Defender suit as well as several other smaller quests scattered around the map. You can also complete activities at Camp Bravo for the military and the Liberty Science HQ for reputation with each faction. Be warned though Liberty and the Military do not get along and earning rep with one will automatically lower your rep with the other. Choose your side carefully or go it alone!

[h2]Improvements to AI[/h2]

Part 2 will feature the large AI overhaul that I have been promising and will my entire focus once part 1 is released however part 1 does still include some out of combat improvements to the AI. The idle code has been cleaned up and improved meaning AI will be more dynamic and active when out of combat. This will result in seeing more movement from the AI around the map. On top of this they can also now loot fallen enemies even beating you to it meaning you may have to kill whoever looted the body you wanted to get the items. There are also several new idle animations to add to the feeling of the NPC's actually doing things outside of combat. Stay tuned for part 2's new soon to discuss the big changes coming to combat AI behaviour!

[h2]What's next[/h2]

As I have mentioned a few times now this is the part 1 release of Unknown Origins. Going forward you will start to see far more regular content and bug fix patches as well as the part 2 release very soon! I want to make sure I am getting content out more regularly meaning I will be sticking with the title Unknown Origins for a while and releasing new content under this name. I can't wait for you all to jump and try out the new content and to get even more coming out soon! Thank you to you all for being so patient with me, this update has grown in size far beyond the original scope but hopefully it's worth it! 

Speak to you all again very soon.

notes.title: Fargone in May
notes.content:
Hi everyone, we have now entered May and I am still working on finishing up the update that is honestly closer to an expansion at this point. I do not usually like to mention the work situation as I don't like to use it as an excuse however many of you know I am a solo developer with a full-time job and lately, the pressure has been high on both work and work on the game. That being said things are close and going very well! I also want to take a moment to talk about what's been finished this week and what's left to do.

[h1]Voice acting[/h1]
In the last few weeks, I have added some new features such as some voice-acted lines for NPCs during combat and idle situations. In combat particularly this helps add to the dynamics of getting into a firefight with another faction or bandits. This is something that has been requested a few times so I am very happy to say it has now been implemented.

[h1]New areas[/h1]
The final set of locations within the Plains has now been wrapped up. The two new additions from the last week are a quarantine campsite and a large factory.

[h1]Gear weight system[/h1]
This is not finished yet but is very close. Gear weight is a new system I am working on to give greater flexibility when choosing your equipment as opposed to simply clicking the one with the highest protection. Now when equipping gear you will get a total gear weight bar that indicates how much your movement speed is affected by the currently equipped gear. You might want to store up some heavy gear for a big raid but swap it out for a lighter set of gear when exploring. This system is also planned to be expanded in the future with faction disguises.

[h1]Custom composed music[/h1]
Another thing I am very excited to add to the game is some completely custom ambience tracks when exploring. The game already features some ambience tracks however they are mainly basic ambience tracks bought online early in development. As of Unknown Origins I have worked with a very talented composer and he has created some amazing tracks that add a lot to the atmosphere of the game.

So what's left? Currently, the main two things are quests and bug fixes. I am considering releasing the update in two parts to allow everyone to jump into the new areas sooner as I am aware I am taking longer than planned with this and I don't like keeping you all waiting. I am going to update everyone this Friday on the release structure for this update and hopefully finally get you all into the new content!

Thank you again for being so patient with me, I hate waiting too so I completely understand all of you asking where the update is!

notes.title: Fargone Unknown Origins update news
notes.content:
Hi everyone, just a short post today to keep you all updated on Fargone's upcoming update Unknown Origins. This update is going to cover two new additions/improvements coming with this update as well as a quick announcement on the release.

I will have to start with the main point and the thing I did not want to do but need to, the update is going to be delayed by a week or two. It will still release in April however this update is huge, closer to an expansion. The new area is exactly half the size of the base games map but is far more densely packed with interesting locations, all of which are now completely custom models. Content-wise this update is also larger than the base game, when you put together the new enemies, new locations, liberty's character variants, missions etc... the total amount of playable content is more than the initial release. I am extremely happy with the current progress which is the reason I have delayed the release to ensure that the content is as well polished as can be and right now that needs some more work. Now that I have announced this delay I want to share a few more things coming with the update, again this is still not everything, I am drip-feeding info to try and keep some things secret!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/e1653478359ab3c61e415b604eb23320c4fc57a4.png[/img]

[h2]Enhanced AI[/h2]

One of the initial goals of Fargone was to create interesting AI that lives and shares the world with the player. With this update, I have started the first step at overhauling and upgrading the AI. This step is focusing on the AI life side of things. The first thing I noticed was a large problem with how the AI handled changing tasks and making decisions. They would very frequently become locked after completing their first decision leaving them to stand idle essentially forever until the game was reloaded. This has now been resolved and has a huge impact on making camps and roaming AI feel less static. While reworking this part of the AI I also added new idle animations and movement animations. AI will now do more than simply stand and smoke, they may pull out a data pad and start planning their next move, loot nearby corpses or just have a snack. This is only the beginning of the plans for the AI but still a very nice step in the direction I always wanted them to be.

[h2]Weather & Sky[/h2]

Weather is something I love in games and although I am happy that Fargone has dynamic weather and a day-night cycle, I still have a lot I want to add. Unknown Origins will introduce several new features such as dynamic fog, toxic rain storms and enhanced audio and sound effects. Starting with fog, although the fog has always been volumetric and relatively nice looking, it was completely static. With the improvements coming you will now see fog density and even colour change depending on the weather which leads perfectly to toxic storms. A new weather variant can now happen at random, the toxic storm will change the entire sky to a dark green with the rain matching. The fog will also gradually change colour and build in thickness making visibility hard, and to top things off, you will need to find shelter during these storms to avoid taking radiation damage from the falling rain and fog. This adds a new survival element as well as a nice view depending on your feelings towards toxic radiation! Supporting these changes is also enhanced audio. New sounds will play across The Barrens and for the first time, these sounds will dynamically change based on the time of day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/81c5df19c1cee5006c864f1b1aa0ace92c56ffe3.png[/img]

This is again a very small update mainly just to announce the release date change but I also wanted to through in a few small bits of information as well! I appreciate everyone being so patient with me as many of you know I am a solo developer with a full-time job so things can take longer than I would like at times but I hope you all really enjoy this update when it releases later in the month! One final note, after having an open discussion with the community within the Discord on the general opinion of options to help fund the game and by extension me working on the game, I have decided to open a Patreon. I will not be pushing this aggressively it is purely an option for those that have asked, I am open to any feedback on the tiers/rewards and just general feedback on making this fair and reasonable. For transparency reasons, the sales of the game go directly back into the game, the reason Unknown Origins contains entirely custom 3d models, textures and characters is due to having a budget from sales. The Patreon is to help me move towards full-time on the game to help create better content faster.

Patreon: patreon.com/RedDotGames

notes.title: Unknown Origins coming April
notes.content:
Hi everyone! First things first I want to say thank you for being patient with me on this update as it has taken a fair amount of time.

It's time to talk new update with Fargone Unkown Origins! Today's post does not go over everything that's coming as this update is a big one but some of the bigger bits and generally what to expect. Much more information will be revealed between now and the release!

Summary: Step into new lands within Unknown Origins and discover the mystery behind Liberty's disappearance and their experiments that have unleashed a new enemy within The Barrens.

[h2]New faction : Liberty[/h2]

With Unknown Origins comes the long-awaited Liberty faction. These guys mean business and utilise cutting-edge equipment far more resistant than most other items currently found within The Barrens. Liberty occupies a new region known as the Plains and has many structures and buildings completely unique to them. As mentioned within the current lore, Liberty is not hostile to begin with, although cautious of outsiders they can be reasoned with and even allied with should the player be willing to work with them for long enough. Liberty also utilises various weapons that are completely new to Fargone with some examples being the PM-90 (P90), MGK (Heavy machine gun), the Mk14 marksman rifle and many more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/3c69ec9ddd5c502b614dd22f937eaeaee9502ddb.png[/img]

[h2]New region : The Plains[/h2]

The Plains is the most detailed and packed environment within Fargone featuring entirely custom locations & models all built specifically for Fargone marking the first steps to moving entirely away from assets. Within the Plains, you will find various locations such as the misty forest, train yards, liberty base, research outpost and much more. I will not be sharing every location today to keep some a mystery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/6f42989ee87e231b0307e76abbd0819acccd67e2.png[/img]

[h2]New Enemies : Mutants[/h2]

Unknown Origins marks the introduction of a new class of enemies that I have wanted in the game for a long time, mutants. Mutants are a result of experiments carried out by Liberty and can be found roaming the world with Liberty re-emergence. These creatures are far more deadly than the average undead and will pose an even greater challenge for the living

[h3]The Scratcher[/h3]

A side effect of the nuclear disaster, the Scratcher is a highly mutated rat with vicious claws. With their fast-moving speed and small size, these mutated creatures are hard to spot and very dangerous, especially within darker areas. They are mostly found within the underground sections of The Barrens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/fbfacaf1212b47738527fb003ef61d592d3f421a.png[/img]

[h3]The Grabber[/h3]

The bigger of the two new mutants and one of the most deadly creatures to ever inhabit the Barrens. Grabbers are a result of Liberty's experiments to harness the power of the undead infection. These beings stalk darker areas and can be heard with muffled sounds. The right arm can be stretched far out to grab their targets making them dangerous from even far ranges. They often will seek cover and hide between attacks waiting for the perfect time. These creatures are not to be taken lightly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/c12d32220b4dd0f053ac936777c156b7bf16f0c3.png[/img]

[h3]New Missions[/h3]

Unknown origins will mark the beginning of adding a larger amount of missions for players to take on. These missions will range from simple tasks such as helping someone out with a delivery, assassination etc..., to larger narrative events that unravel the story of what Liberty has been doing in hiding and how the mutants came to be. There will be lots more info to share in the future on missions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/a9f997e001b793dc40b42e5adc7329d723f4bc00.png[/img]

[h3]New equipment & Armour upgrading[/h3]

Unknown origins will bring with it over 60 new items to collect within the world including some new useful pieces of equipment such as the binoculars and night vision goggles. As well as this players will be able to interact with a new NPC that will allow them to upgrade armour pieces with useful enhancements. As with Trials Of The Hollowed, more weapons have now received the new animation treatment and will look far better as a result.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/0f26ee7c6756983bd7a97f304ded80ffaf051ce4.png[/img]

[h3]New features[/h3]

Many of the features will be kept quiet until they are more polished and ready for show however one big addition to the game is the addition of swimming. Swimming allows for better traversal of the map and removes many of the invisible barriers allowing greater freedom in the open world. The goal is to give players as many routes around the map as possible both for travel and planning engagements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43315919/ca6ccd7a36738e1d33be839d3c66ddcd27411668.png[/img]

This update will also bring a very large amount of bug fixes and community requested features such as the ability to see what attachments are equipped to a weapon from within the inventory, overhauled datapad UI system and some very large AI improvements to name a few.

This just scratching the surface of what's coming with this update and I will be sharing more as we progress closer to the release. I hope you enjoyed this first peak into the future of Fargone and as always a massive thank you to everyone who has played the game. 

See you in The Barrens!
